title: Strong earthquake shakes Panama, prompting tsunami alert
summary: Tremors were felt in the capital city when a powerful earthquake shook Panama, triggering a tsunami threat warning in Central and South America.

image.caption: The earthquake shook buildings in Panama City, the capital of Panama [FILE: March 2026]Image: Martin Bernetti/AFP

blocks.text: A powerful magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck Panamaon Friday morning.
According to the US Geological Survey, the quake's epicenter was located approximately 10 kilometers (6 miles) southwest of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba, near Panama's southern tip.
The quake struck at a depth of 10 kilometers (6 miles).
Tremors shook Panama City, causing buildings to shake and prompting people to evacuate into the streets.

blocks.caption: The earthquake sent people in Panama City outdoors Image: Enea Lebrun/REUTERS

blocks.text: "We felt it very strongly. It knocked things over in the kitchen, but we're okay, though we're very scared," Rosendo Domínguez, 60, who is from Herrera province, where the earthquake struck, told The Associated Press by phone. “Everyone is outside, scared."
Shortly after the quake, aftershocks continued to shake the streets on Friday.

Meanwhile, the US Tsunami Warning System issued an alert stating that hazardous tsunami waves were possible along parts of the coasts of Panama, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador, and Mexico within the next three hours.
The system also reported a tsunami threat to Hawaii.
Initially, there were no reports of damage to the Panama Canal. The Panama Canal Authority stated that the waterway was operating as usual.
Panama is located along the "Ring of Fire," a line of seismic faults encircling the Pacific Ocean where most of the world's earthquakes occur.
